title: Clinical Evaluation of ONE-X Versus Boston XO Rigid Gas-Permeable Contact Lenses
official: Clinical Evaluation of the Safety and Performance of a New Material for Rigid Gas-Permeable Contact Lenses: A Randomized Comparative Study With Boston XO
summary:
This study compares two materials used to make rigid gas-permeable contact lenses, a type of hard lens that allows oxygen to pass through to the eye. The materials are ONE-X, a new material being studied, and Boston XO, a material already used in contact lenses. Both sets of lenses have the same Elipsys STD design. The study aims to find out how comfortable the lenses are at the end of the day, how well they work, and whether they cause any eye problems during wear.

The study plans to enroll 24 adults in Bilbao, Spain. Each participant will wear both types of lenses in both eyes, one type at a time. The order will be assigned at random. Participants will wear each type for 30 days, with a two-day break between periods when they will not wear either set of study lenses. Participants and the clinicians assessing the study outcomes will not know which material is being worn during each period.

The main measure is how comfortable the lenses feel at the end of the day after 30 days of wearing each type. Participants will rate their comfort on a scale from 1 to 10, with higher scores indicating greater comfort. The study team will also check vision, lens fit, and eye health, and will record any symptoms or adverse events.

interventions.name: Elipsys STD Contact Lenses Made From ONE-X
Elipsys STD Contact Lenses Made From Boston XO

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older.
* Able to understand the study and its procedures and provide written informed consent.
* Myopia and/or hyperopia, with or without corneal astigmatism, that can be corrected with Elipsys STD lenses within the available manufacturing ranges.
* Regular corneas suitable for fitting with Elipsys STD corneal rigid gas-permeable contact lenses.
* Corneal astigmatism of 2.00 diopters (D) or less.
* Corneal and refractive characteristics compatible with the available Elipsys STD lens parameters: base curve radius 7.40 to 8.50 mm, diameter 9.00 to 12.00 mm, and spherical power -25.00 to +25.00 D.
* Clinically acceptable fit with Elipsys STD lenses in both eyes according to the protocol.
* Corrected visual acuity sufficient for reliable assessment of visual performance.
* No active ocular condition that contraindicates rigid gas-permeable contact lens wear.
* Willing to wear the study lenses as instructed and maintain similar wearing conditions in both study periods.
* Willing to use only the lens care system specified in the protocol unless otherwise directed by the investigator.
* Able and willing to complete both 30-day wear periods, the two-day washout, all six study visits, and the required assessments and questionnaires.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Active ocular disease that may contraindicate or interfere with safe contact lens wear.
* Infection, inflammation, or clinically significant abnormality of the cornea, conjunctiva, eyelids, or anterior segment at enrollment.
* Keratoconus, pellucid marginal degeneration, corneal ectasia, significant corneal irregularity, or another condition requiring a lens design other than Elipsys STD.
* Corneal astigmatism outside the indicated range for Elipsys STD or any refractive or corneal characteristic that prevents a clinically acceptable fit.
* Clinically significant corneal staining, redness, infiltrates, edema, neovascularization, or another ocular finding at baseline that, in the investigator's judgment, may compromise participant safety or interfere with interpretation of the results.
* Prior corneal or refractive surgery resulting in corneal changes that are incompatible with the planned lens fit or may interfere with interpretation of the results.
* Use of topical ocular medication that may affect the ocular surface or tear film during the study, except for products specifically permitted by the investigator.
* Use of systemic medication or an uncontrolled systemic disease that, in the investigator's judgment, may significantly affect the ocular surface, tear film, or safety of contact lens wear.
* Known hypersensitivity, allergy, or intolerance to any component of the study lenses or lens care solutions.
* Concurrent participation in another clinical investigation that may compromise participant safety or interfere with interpretation of the results.
* Any circumstance that, in the investigator's judgment, makes adherence to lens wear and care instructions or attendance at scheduled visits unlikely.
* A clinical circumstance associated with pregnancy or breastfeeding that, in the investigator's judgment, may affect the safety of lens wear or interpretation of the results. Pregnancy and breastfeeding alone do not exclude participation.
